Every number here comes from a result file committed in the repository (`engine/ts/packages/bench/results`). The current figures are from `matrix-2026-10-31.json`, produced by `engine/ts/packages/bench/src/matrix.ts` (re-run with `RUNS=9 CLI_RUNS=5 node packages/bench/src/matrix.ts` in `engine/ts`).

**Machine.** Intel(R) Xeon(R) Processor @ 2.10GHz, 4 logical CPUs, 16 GiB, Linux 6.18.44-fc-v185 x64, 2026-10-31. **Versions.** Node v22.23.4 (V8 12.4.254.21-node.57); Bun 1.4.4 (JavaScriptCore); rustc 1.97.0 (2d8144b78 2026-07-07).

**Noise.** A shared 4-vCPU cloud VM: other tenants share the CPUs, so individual timings vary (up to about 2x between runs on this VM). Each e2e figure is from fresh processes, original and compiled interleaved; best (min) is the most stable figure, median shows the spread. Treat differences under about 10% as noise.

## Whole programs: original vs Viscosity, Node and Bun

Each program's own timed section (performance.now()), 9 fresh processes per version per runtime, original and compiled interleaved, after one discarded run of each. Compiled with the TS engine (default options); the Rust CLI's output is compared too.

Best of 9 (median in brackets), milliseconds of each program's timed section; speed-up = original / Viscosity.

| program | layout | Node original | Node Viscosity | Node speed-up | Bun original | Bun Viscosity | Bun speed-up |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| boids | `fl=soa` | 57.4 (68.6) | 43.8 (56.6) | **1.31×** (1.21×) | 64.1 (75.4) | 34.6 (49.7) | **1.85×** (1.52×) |
| heat | `cells=soa` | 352.4 (407.3) | 85.7 (93.6) | **4.11×** (4.35×) | 96.4 (102.6) | 94.5 (118.9) | **1.02×** (0.86×) |
| ledger | `tx=soa` | 167.5 (198.3) | 44.6 (48.7) | **3.75×** (4.08×) | 117.5 (126.1) | 40.8 (52.4) | **2.88×** (2.41×) |
| nbody | `bs=soa` | 61.6 (71.3) | 51.3 (63.5) | **1.2×** (1.12×) | 50 (62.8) | 51.6 (55.3) | **0.97×** (1.13×) |
| particles | `ps=soa` | 393 (423.3) | 90 (114) | **4.37×** (3.71×) | 155.2 (178.9) | 51.7 (56.6) | **3×** (3.16×) |
| **geometric mean** | | | | **2.54×** (2.46×) | | | **1.74×** (1.62×) |

The original and compiled programs' checksums matched on every run, and each program printed the same checksum on Node and on Bun. The Rust CLI's compiled code is byte-identical to the TypeScript engine's for every program. Bun relative to Node (geometric mean of Node best / Bun best; above 1 means Bun is faster): original programs 1.71×, compiled programs 1.17×.

## Compile speed: Rust CLI vs TypeScript CLI

Method: `viscosity build <file>` to stdout, one fresh process per compile, 5 runs each, alternating TS and Rust. Wall time of the whole process, from Node's child_process.

**Over the 40-program corpus (sum of medians): TypeScript CLI 4764.6 ms, Rust CLI 435.8 ms, 10.9× faster.** Outputs were byte-identical for every program.

**In process.** compile() in one Node process: 50 warm-up calls, then 200 timed calls per program. TS: the reference engine from source; Rust: @viscosity/wasm (nodejs target) on the same Node. Total of medians: TypeScript 14979.7 µs, Rust as WebAssembly 2846.8 µs, 5.26× faster.

Per-program figures are in `matrix-2026-10-31.md`.
